origins.note: Sherrill says its stainless is melted and made in the United States. Company statement, not a mill certificate.

statusNote: Owens named Allegheny Ludlum as a mill the steel could come from (2015). That is an example, not a named supplier. Pittsburgh, named in 2021, fits Allegheny Ludlum's home region but no source ties ATI to Sherrill.

sources.title: Liberty Sets the Table for Growth
sources.note: Greg Owens: Sherrill requires mill reports showing steel melted and manufactured in the United States, and says it "could come from Allegheny Ludlum, it could come from AK Steel, and it could come from NASS, or another place down in Birmingham." These are examples, not a named supplier for any heat.

sources.title: Sellers of American-made goods are thriving amid supply-chain chaos
sources.note: Owens: products start as a coil or bar of steel made in one of three places: Western New York, Pittsburgh, or Tennessee. Packaging is locally sourced. No mill named.

sources.title: Sherrill Manufacturing
sources.note: Roberts: steel was made in Pittsburgh, Tennessee or Alabama. Packaging materials come from a family-owned company in Earlville, NY (not named). Buffing compounds come from Utica and Detroit (suppliers not named).

sources.title: Liberty Tabletop responds to expanded US tariffs, confirms 100% US-made supply chain
sources.note: Company statement: steel poured and forged in America; packaging sourced and produced in the United States. No supplier named.
